_metadata.description: P2 requirements — expansion beyond one household on one instance, including the deliberate crossing into real value and the unification with treasury's mandate contract.

requirements.title: The system may settle grants through a chain-backed rail behind the existing grant contract.
requirements.description: A real-value rail may be added as an adapter behind the same grant contract, with the local rail remaining first-class rather than becoming a fallback. Crossing this line re-opens questions P0 deliberately closed: key custody, irreversible loss, and whether holding value for other holders on one instance constitutes a regulated activity. None of those may be answered implicitly by shipping the adapter; each requires a recorded decision in docs/internal/DECISIONS.md first, and the no-monetary-value structural test from TKE-P0-014 must be consciously amended rather than deleted.

validation.notes: Gated on a recorded custody and regulatory decision before any implementation work begins.

requirements.title: The system may recognize token types across Vrooli instances relayed through vrooli-bridge.
requirements.description: Two households, or one household across two machines, may share a token type. Trust must be relayed through vrooli-bridge rather than established by direct peer connection, consistent with the ecosystem's position that tier-to-tier communication goes through the bridge. Cross-instance events must remain journaled locally so a bridge outage degrades reach without corrupting history.

validation.notes: Deferred until a second instance is a real operator need rather than a hypothetical.

requirements.title: The system may support listings and offers between holders subject to minter policy.
requirements.description: A marketplace extends transfer into price discovery: a holder lists something, another offers, and the minter's policy bounds what is tradeable. This may reuse the reservation mechanism so a listed item is not double-committed. It should not be built before transfer has run in a real household, because a marketplace over an economy nobody trades in is a surface with no users.

validation.notes: Gated on observed transfer usage in a real household.

requirements.title: The grant and mandate shapes may be extracted into one governed contract shared with treasury.
requirements.description: The two scenarios deliberately ship congruent shapes before sharing one. Unification may happen once both have shipped enough to know what is genuinely common rather than coincidentally similar — premature extraction would freeze the wrong abstraction across two products. Until then, congruence is maintained by the parity test in TKE-P0-002 and by recording every intentional divergence.

validation.notes: Gated on treasury shipping its mandate contract and on both scenarios having real usage.

requirements.title: A minter may delegate minting or approval authority within limits that can only narrow.
requirements.description: A second adult may mint or approve within bounds the primary minter sets. Delegation must be one-way narrowing — a delegate can never hold authority the delegator does not, and never outlive it — which is the same attenuation the ecosystem already applies to agent scopes in agent-manager. This should reuse that semantic rather than inventing a second delegation model.

validation.notes: Deferred until a two-minter household is a real need; must reuse existing attenuation semantics.

requirements.title: The system may support non-transferable tokens that can be earned and displayed but never redeemed.
requirements.description: Recognition economies differ from reward economies: an achievement should be visible and permanent rather than spendable. A non-transferable, non-redeemable token class may express that, reusing the mint and journal spine while declining the transfer and redemption paths. This is the smallest possible extension that turns the scenario into a recognition tool for teams as well as a reward tool for households.

validation.notes: Deferred; validated by a team using it for recognition rather than by a household.

requirements.title: The console may surface earning and redemption patterns over time.
requirements.description: A minter may want to know whether the economy is inflating, stalling, or rewarding what they intended. Analytics are a projection over the journal like any balance, so they may be added without new storage. They should describe rather than prescribe — the product does not tell a household how to run its economy, and any framing that scores a holder's behavior is out of scope.

validation.notes: Deferred until an economy has enough history for a trend to be meaningful.
